title: [CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-80188 — The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass…
summary: The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

title: [CVSS 8.1 HIGH] CVE-2026-126716 — The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic …
summary: The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-76540 — In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user …
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles can configure a metric alert through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that runs a search with elevated privileges. The vulnerability lets the user access or modify data and disrupt the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability occurs because Splunk Enterprise does not enforce the required role-based authorization when it processes metric alert configuration through the REST API. Splunk Enterprise schedules the resulting search with elevated authorization and runs attacker-controlled search processing with that authorization.
For more information see About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR can bind existing cross-repository playbook references to a different source control repository when a deleted repository name is reused.

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-131271 — In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to vi…

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-131269 — In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit…

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-131263 — In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps…

This could let the user modify files used by Splunk SOAR and execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR constructs the dependency installation command from app-supplied metadata without preventing that metadata from changing its arguments.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

title: [CVSS 9.1 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-131202 — In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_ad…

title: [CVSS 9.1 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-104099 — Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul.…
summary: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.

title: [CVSS 8.2 HIGH] CVE-2026-130886 — @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HT…
summary: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions 12.8.1 through 12.8.3, its buildURL function checked the attacker-supplied source string for parent-directory segments, but when the source begins with the same special scheme as the base, such as http or https, the WHATWG URL parser drops the scheme and resolves the remainder as a relative path. A payload that glues the scheme to a percent-encoded parent-directory sequence therefore passes the check, because the inspected segment reads as the scheme plus the dots rather than a bare parent-directory token, while the proxy forwards the encoded traversal unchanged. An upstream that percent-decodes the request path before resolving dot-segments then serves a path outside the configured prefix, so an unauthenticated client scoped to an upstream prefix, or relying on Fastify route guards in front of the proxy, can escape that prefix and reach sibling or parent upstream endpoints. The per-segment check added in 12.8.1 is what the scheme prefix bypasses, and releases up to 12.8.0 already rejected the decoded form. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

title: [CVSS 8.1 HIGH] CVE-2026-104129 — pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postg…
summary: pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

title: [CVSS 8.1 HIGH] CVE-2026-103026 — Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting s…
summary: Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting services. Prior to 1.5.7, the HasConfirmation trait in app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php, included by app/Livewire/Component.php across 36 client-facing Livewire components, exposed executeConfirmedAction as a public action that invoked any component method accepted by method_exists. The action could call inherited InteractsWithProperties::fill(), whose data_set() writes arbitrary public properties, including state marked with #[Locked] and dotted paths into hydrated Eloquent models. Depending on the methods and properties exposed by an individual component, an unauthenticated caller could use this path to bypass intended authorization and modify server-side state intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.7.

title: [CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-128138 — NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data s…
summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

title: [CVSS 9.6 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-77369 — Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generi…
summary: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not authorize the database resource selected by a typename.referenceId.columnName room name. The YJS initial-content provider then reads the selected file.* column without CanRead or CanUpdate checks, and bidirectional synchronization allows a low-privileged authenticated user to read or modify restricted row content. Unauthenticated requests are rejected, and standalone non-canonical room names remain shared-by-name rooms. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

title: [CVSS 9.6 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-133189 — A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based stor…

title: [CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-14492 — The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerab…
summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

title: [CVSS 8.0 HIGH] CVE-2026-109555 — The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Ob…
summary: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.
title_ja: 攻撃者たちが Optimizely を使ってトップウェブサイトへのマルウェアテストを実行
summary_ja: 過去24時間以内に、Optimizelyというウェブサイトでユーザー体験をカスタマイズし、新機能をテストするサービスのセキュリティ脆弱性により、少なくとも178のトップウェブサイトが訪問者にさまざまなマルウェアの悪用を無意識に提供した。専門家によると、BBC、CNN、Equifax、Ledger、Zoomなどのサイトにデータを盗み取る悪意あるソフトウェアが静かに注入されたこの事件は、多くのサイトがその脆弱性を認識していない現実によって悪化した。
